rationale: This is the ninth instance of the archive's exhausted "quality-deterioration × (sstk+dltis)/at" template — differing only in the conditioning variable, which itself (rising current assets relative to sales) is essentially the well-known working-capital-accrual/net-operating-asset anomaly, and the near-identical "Working Capital Equity Reliance" already tested a lct/sale variant.

This is a cosmetic level-to-trend substitution on the archived "Low Coverage Forced Paydown" (same NEG(coverage) conditioner, identical dltr/at financing leg), and the bearish-debt-retirement premise also runs against the standard net-debt-issuance anomaly direction without any new argument for why paydown should be bad.

Quality-conditioned buyback signals were already tested twice in the archive ("Persistent Cash Profit Buyback Confirmation," "Quality Deleveraging Buyback"), both with essentially zero FF5 alpha, and the only change here is swapping the net-repurchase leg for a rank-spread against total external financing — a recombination rather than a diagnosis of why the long leg failed.

The financing-mix spread (debt reliance versus equity reliance) is a substantively different construct from the archived maintenance-burden × issuance-level signals, and the archive's counterintuitive positive alpha on high-dp/sale equity issuers gives a coherent reason to expect the debt-minus-equity tilt to price negatively — though the proposal should have stated that diagnosis explicitly.

This is a near-duplicate of the archived "External Funding Payout Retrenchment" (identical three legs) with a one-period LAG applied to the payout-change term, which is a cosmetic timing tweak rather than a new mechanism.

The signal simply splices the conditioner from "Low Coverage Forced Paydown" onto the exact MIN(lagged dltr, dltis) financing leg from "Failed Deleveraging Reborrower" — a mechanical recombination of two archived signals, and the parent's Fama-MacBeth slope pointed the wrong way, which this proposal does not address.
